simple.meaning: קָרַס (qâraç) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to hunch , i.e. be hump-backed.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 46:1. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָרַס (H7164) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: קָרַס (qâraç) / H7164 is traced through Isaiah 46:1, Isaiah 46:2 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7164. qaras [ קָרַס ] verb bend down, stoop, crouch (intransitive) (compare perhaps Arabic disc, round cake ; compare Late Hebrew קַרְצוּלָא קַרְסוּלָּא, ᵑ7 קַרְצוֺל, קַרְסוֺל, all ankle ); — Qal Perfect 3plural קָֽרְסוּ Isa 46:2 ; Participle קֹרֵס 46:1 (both + כָּרַע ); of vanquished gods of Babylon.
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; properly, to protrude ; used only as denominative from 7165 (for alliteration with 7167 ),

occurrences.englishText: They stoop and they bow down together.
